requirements.requirement: Keep application data under /srv/data recoverable through a filesystem snapshot.
requirements.summary: A dedicated Btrfs filesystem was persistently mounted at /srv, /srv/data was created as a subvolume, and a read-only snapshot was captured at /srv/.snapshots/data-before-change. The snapshot and filesystem remained healthy and available after restart.

requirements.requirement: Modify /srv/data after capturing the earlier snapshot.
requirements.summary: After snapshot creation, the executor changed one file, deleted another, added a transient file, and directly demonstrated checksum divergence from the captured baseline.

requirements.requirement: Restore the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot.
requirements.summary: The live subvolume was recreated from the preserved snapshot. All three baseline SHA-256 checks passed, the restored tree and modes matched the baseline, the transient file was absent, and snapshot ancestry identified the earlier snapshot as the parent. The same restored state was verified after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot ID, and recovered mount, data, snapshot, filesystem, and system state were all observed. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear roles: filesystem provisioning and persistence (cmd-9062568d9c7d45b5), baseline data and snapshot creation (cmd-281fe58ba2fc4dd3), the contract-required post-snapshot modification (cmd-56ef8e3ac8a44a74), restoration (cmd-710ea9addc014686), and the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-3d0225b134c34d9f). No unnecessary mutation was identified. After execution there were no failed services, new listeners, package-health damage, or executor-created temporary residue; the changed systemd-private paths were normal consequences of reboot.
